A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CCPS research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original confidence-estimation experiments across four LLMs and three MMLU variants, with aggregate results, calibration plots, and SHAP analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds MedMCQA results, self-consistency comparisons, token-masking experiments, and feature ablations.

M1.justification: The frozen-LLM perturbation procedure, 75-feature representation, MC/OE architectures, and two-stage training remain unchanged. The added loss formula and feature accounting document the existing approach without establishing a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Appendix I adds MedMCQA evaluation in multiple-choice and open-ended formats. This extends existing medical and general QA coverage; the CT training datasets and original MMLU evaluations are retained.

E2.justification: Self-Consistency is newly evaluated across all four LLMs and three MMLU variants in Appendix K.2 and Table 17. The existing comparator set remains present in the original benchmark comparisons.

E3.justification: New evaluation protocols include token-feature zeroing with POS grouping, controlled 12/63/75-feature comparisons, and 75 distinct feature-removal retrainings per LLM. These substantially expand the experimental controls. Original benchmark settings and metrics remain unchanged; self-consistency sampling details are incomplete.

E4.justification: Appendices K.1, K.3, and K.5 add tests of content-word sensitivity, perturbation versus original-feature contributions, and individual-feature importance through removal and retraining. These extend substantially beyond v1's SHAP analysis, which is retained as K.4.

E5.justification: The existing mean ± standard-deviation tables are unchanged. No new seed counts, confidence intervals, or specified significance tests appear. Token-masking effects are called statistically significant without a reported testing procedure; the 75 retrainings represent distinct ablation conditions.

E6.justification: Original MMLU scores are retained, while Tables 12 and 16–19 add substantial results. For example, MedMCQA multiple-choice Llama ECE is 26.8 for CT versus 11.0 for CCPS; Qwen-14B MMLU-Pro ablation ECE is 21.0, 11.0, and 4.2 for original-only, perturbation-only, and full features.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 adds an explicit mathematical definition of the previously named max-margin loss. Its self-distance term, ||e+ - e+||, is identically zero and does not support the accompanying claim of pulling correct embeddings together. Existing perturbation mathematics remains unchanged; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same methodological, efficiency, generalizability, and calibration/discrimination claims, including the headline improvement figures.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations concerning semantic token prioritization, perturbation features as the principal performance driver, complementary feature groups, and changing confidence signals with task difficulty. It also interprets MedMCQA results as supporting medical-domain generalization. The existing limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 explains the fixed perturbation hyperparameter choices and feature-vector composition more explicitly. However, it removes v1's disclosures of Unsloth model versions, non-quantized handling, bfloat16 precision, and Transformers/PyTorch usage. Architecture, hardware, and code/data access information otherwise remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds Pal et al. for MedMCQA and Xiong et al. for self-consistency, strengthening the explicit comparison with output-consensus approaches. Several model and software references disappear with the removed language-model paragraph; the broader related-work framing is retained.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites clarify perturbation choices, evaluation metrics, and semantic grading. New appendices reorganize supplementary material, including moving SHAP into the ablation section. Author/contact and acknowledgment text also change, while the main narrative structure remains recognizable.

P2.justification: Table 1 changes from a narrow vertical arrangement to a full-width layout pairing models side by side. Five supplementary tables are added, and existing tables are renumbered. All 34 figures are retained unchanged apart from their placement and surrounding page formatting.

improvement.justification: The controlled feature-group and removal ablations substantially address v1's weak attribution of gains to perturbations, previously supported mainly by SHAP and comparisons with different methods. Self-consistency and MedMCQA evaluations further strengthen the empirical case. These gains outweigh limited documentation losses and new weaknesses, including the inconsistent loss explanation, underspecified sampling protocol, and unsupported statistical-significance wording.
